rationale: The user asked for this follow-up round and named one priority: the statutory accounts of Foot Locker Europe B.V. (Utrecht, KvK 23067735). Under FL's transfer-pricing model, local country entities (FL UK, FL Germany KG) are limited-risk distributors on a fixed 2-4% margin, and FL Europe B.V. is the principal that bears EMEA retail risk, so that is where the European losses sit. Task 1 is therefore a full, free-source hunt for those accounts, the Dutch side of the cross-border merger, and the 2026-10-02 management change. Wave 1 of this cluster ran press scoops, buyers, competition filings, people/jobs, company-side news and digital/brand signals: no sale process, adviser or bidder was found, plus a pattern of DKS people taking over EMEA boards. tasks.title: Foot Locker Europe B.V. (Utrecht, KvK 23067735): annual accounts, 403 status, merger papers and the 2026-10-02 management change
tasks.instructions:
PRIORITY TASK, requested directly by the analyst. Find, and if possible read, the statutory annual accounts (jaarrekening) of Foot Locker Europe B.V., Stationsplein 32, Utrecht (KvK 23067735). WHY: FL Europe runs a principal/limited-risk-distributor transfer-pricing model. Foot Locker U.K. Ltd's accounts state that retail risk is borne by Foot Locker Europe B.V. under a Distribution and Service Agreement, and the UK group earns a set margin (4.2% gross margin in FY2024). Foot Locker Germany GmbH & Co. KG is a contract distributor keeping a fixed ~2-3% EBIT. The country entities therefore look profitable, and the true EMEA P&L and losses sit in FL Europe B.V. DKS guides a 27-29% tax rate because of 'Europe losses with valuation allowances'. Theses: (1) DKS will sell, license or exit FL Europe; (2) European closures are running above consensus (Bloomberg holds FL Europe at ~550 stores flat through FY32; DKS reported 559 at 8/1/26).

ALREADY KNOWN (do not report as novel): the 403/limited-risk language in the FL UK accounts; Company.info flags a management change at FL Europe B.V. dated 2026-10-02 but the names are behind a paywall; FL Europe B.V. is the President (corporate officer) of FL France Holdings SAS (register entry 23-Sep-2026); Foot Locker Europe Holdings SLU (Spain) was merged into Foot Locker Dutch Holdings B.V. (KvK 84791446), with draft terms dated 2026-03-20 and the Spanish dissolution registered 2026-08-28; the Dutch Staatscourant has no notice; the FootLocker Europe.com B.V. imprint (KvK 30181126) is unchanged.

STEPS:
(1) KvK free information. Using a real browser tool if one is available (kvk.nl/zoeken is a JavaScript app), open the free company page and the KvK product/order page (the 'Jaarrekening' and 'Deponeringen' product lists, which show for free which filings exist before you pay) for each of: Foot Locker Europe B.V. (23067735), Foot Locker Dutch Holdings B.V. (84791446), FLE Holdings Cooperatief U.A. (30184448), Foot Locker Netherlands B.V. (23063181), FootLocker Europe.com B.V. (30181126) and FLE Logistics B.V. (14123551; a new filing dated 2026-04-28 was seen in wave 1, so find out what it is). For each, record: every deposited financial-year document (jaarrekening/annual accounts, 403-verklaring [art. 2:403 BW parent-guarantee declaration], intrekking 403 [withdrawal], 404 notice, consolidated accounts of a foreign parent deposited under 403, fusievoorstel/voorstel tot grensoverschrijdende fusie [merger proposal], toelichting [explanatory report], fusie-akte [merger deed]) with its financial year, deposit date and price. Also record the number of vestigingen (branches) and the SBI activity codes. Do NOT buy anything. List each paid document as a lead with its exact KvK product name, year and price, so the analyst can buy it by hand.
(2) Work out which filing regime applies. If FL Europe B.V. relied on a 403 declaration by Foot Locker, Inc., it files no own accounts; the deposit would be FL Inc.'s consolidated accounts. Post-deal, DKS would either deposit a new 403 (Dick's Sporting Goods, Inc. as guarantor, which implies it is keeping and backing the entity) or withdraw it (a classic pre-sale step). Either is a Tier A finding. If FL Europe B.V. files full accounts, the CY2024 accounts should already be deposited (the Dutch deadline is 12 months after year-end, and FL European entities use calendar years) and CY2025 accounts are due by end-2026. Check whether they are already in.
(3) Free mirrors and secondary sources for the numbers. Check northdata.com/.de/.nl (financial key figures, publications and officer timeline), company.info (free teaser: omzet, employees, financial key figures), Graydon/Creditsafe/Dun & Bradstreet free teasers, bedrijfsdata.nl, drimble.nl, oozo.nl, opencorporates, and Google for 'Foot Locker Europe B.V.' with jaarrekening / jaarverslag / 'annual report' / filetype:pdf. Check Dutch financial press that writes up the accounts of large Dutch BVs (Het Financieele Dagblad, Quote, RetailTrends, Twinklemagazine, Fashionunited NL, DUIC, Vastgoedmarkt) for 'Foot Locker Europe' with verlies (loss), omzet (revenue), jaarrekening, afboeking (write-down), reorganisatie or '2024'/'2025'. Also search for Dutch fiscal-unity, APA or tax-ruling references to FL Europe.
(4) Identify the people behind the 2026-10-02 change without paying. Where FL Europe B.V. is a corporate officer of a foreign subsidiary, the foreign registers often name the natural person who represents it. Check BODACC/annuaire-entreprises entries for FL France Holdings SAS (SIREN 480023324) for the 'representant permanent' (permanent representative) of Foot Locker Europe B.V., BORME entries for the Spanish entities (Foot Locker Spain SL, Hoja B-101890) for 'representante persona fisica', and the Belgian Staatsblad and Italian Registro Imprese summaries. Cross-check with LinkedIn (Matthew Barnes, Reid Sigal, Erik Amperse, Andreas Zipfel, Neil Carter) and with northdata. Report who joined or left the FL Europe B.V. board and when.
(5) Read the Dutch side of the cross-border merger. Find the Foot Locker Dutch Holdings B.V. merger proposal/explanatory report on KvK (a paid lead if needed), any newspaper announcement required under the Dutch implementation of Directive 2019/2121, and whether FLE Holdings Cooperatief U.A. or other Dutch entities have since been merged, dissolved (ontbinding) or set to 'in liquidatie'.
(6) If any accounts are readable (free mirror, cached PDF or press write-up), extract: revenue, gross margin, operating result, net result, store-asset and right-of-use impairments, onerous-lease or restructuring provisions, store counts or closures by country, headcount, intercompany charges/transfer-pricing true-ups paid to country entities, tax losses carried forward and deferred-tax-asset recognition, going-concern language, and post-balance-sheet events (DKS change of control, strategic review, restructuring, intended disposals). Quote the original Dutch/English text.

RULES: no purchases, no login or account creation, no CAPTCHA bypass. If a document is paid, log it as a lead with the exact product and price (the analyst will decide whether to buy). WebSearch/Apify budgets may be low, so go direct to register and mirror URLs. Tier A = KvK register entry or filed document; Tier B = reputable mirror or press citing the filing. A clean null (e.g. 'only a 403 by Foot Locker, Inc. is deposited; no own accounts') is a valid finding: log it with the evidence.

tasks.title: Companies House and CRO filings since 2026-09-15: FL UK CY2025 accounts, accounting-reference-date changes, new charges or officers
tasks.instructions:
GOAL: Find and read any statutory filing made since wave 1 by Foot Locker's UK and Irish entities. The highest value is the CY2025 annual report of Foot Locker U.K. Limited (Companies House 02568406) and of its subsidiary Freedom Sportsline Limited (01779106), the first full-year accounts covering the DKS era. A UK private company with a 31-Dec year-end must file within 9 months, so CY2025 accounts were due by about 30-Sep-2026 unless the accounting reference date was changed. Theses: (1) DKS exit/sale/licensing of FL Europe; (2) European closures above consensus (Bloomberg holds FL Europe at ~550 stores flat through FY32; DKS reported 559 at 8/1/26).

ALREADY KNOWN (not novel): the CY2024 accounts (filed 2025-12-01, signed 2025-11-24): 2 openings and 3 closures in 2025, 1 opening and 3 closures approved for 2026, selling space -8.6%, lease commitments GBP58.8m with GBP6.4m due after 5 years, limited-risk distributor with risk borne by FL Europe B.V., and the only post-balance-sheet event being the DKS change of control; officer changes through Jun-2026 (Barnes, Boylan in and out, Carter, Sen Lonell out, Sigal as secretary); the PSC notice naming DKS as 75%+ controller from 2025-09-08; no charges, CVA or insolvency.

STEPS:
(1) Pull the free Companies House filing history (https://find-and-update.company-information.service.gov.uk/company/02568406/filing-history and /01779106/filing-history; the public JSON API at api.company-information.service.gov.uk needs a free key, so use the HTML pages if you have no key) for every document dated 2026-06-01 to today: AA (accounts), AA01 (change of accounting reference date, e.g. a move to a late-January year-end that matches DKS's fiscal year), CS01 (confirmation statement, which shows shareholders), AP01/TM01/CH01 (officers), MR01 (charges), SH01/SH19 (capital), RES (resolutions), AD01 (registered office) and any DS01/LIQ forms. Do the same for the other UK FL companies you can find via the Companies House officer pages of Reid Sigal and Matthew Barnes (list every UK company they are officers of, with appointment dates).
(2) If new accounts are filed, download the PDF (free) and read the strategic report, directors' report and notes in full. Extract: store openings and closures in 2025 and those planned or approved for 2026-27; any wording on a strategic review, fleet review, 'unproductive assets', impairment of right-of-use assets or fixtures, onerous-lease or dilapidation provisions; changes to the distribution/transfer-pricing agreement with FL Europe B.V.; going-concern basis and any parent support letter (from DKS or FL Europe B.V.); headcount; lease-commitment maturity; and post-balance-sheet events. Quote verbatim. Compare each item with the CY2024 accounts.
(3) If accounts are overdue (no AA by 30-Sep-2026 and no AA01 extension), say so: an overdue filing is itself a signal.
(4) Ireland: on the CRO free search (core.cro.ie) list every submission since 2026-08-01 for Foot Locker Retail Ireland Limited (391370) and FL Finance (Europe) Limited (391464): B1 annual returns with financial statements, B10 officer changes, B2 registered-office changes, merger (CBM) or strike-off forms. Report form types and dates. If financial statements are free to view, read them, especially FL Finance (Europe) Ltd's intercompany loans to and investments in European FL subsidiaries and any impairment of those investments (a direct marker of the value DKS ascribes to EMEA).
(5) Also check the UK gender-pay-gap service (free) for Freedom Sportsline's 2025/26 report (snapshot date 5-Apr-2026): headcount and the named signatory director.

RULES: free official sources only, no login, purchase or CAPTCHA bypass. Tier A = Companies House or CRO document. Log explicit nulls per entity (e.g. 'no filing since 2026-06-19').

tasks.title: DKS securities class action (W.D. Pa. 2:26-cv-01860) and other litigation: confidential-witness and Foot Locker International allegations
tasks.instructions:
GOAL: Read the court documents in the securities class action against DICK'S Sporting Goods filed in the U.S. District Court for the Western District of Pennsylvania (case 2:26-cv-01860, filed about 2026-09-04; lead-plaintiff deadline 2026-11-03). Extract every allegation, confidential-witness (CW) statement and quoted management statement about Foot Locker's international, European, EMEA, Australian/APAC or atmos businesses. Theses: (1) DKS will sell, license or exit FL Europe/APAC; (2) European/APAC FL store closures are above consensus. ALREADY KNOWN (not novel): the complaint quotes Ed Stack saying the clean-out in 'Europe' was 'done'; the deadline is 3-Nov-2026; the public management statements from DKS calls and conferences through 2026-09-14 (Stack's 'creating a menu ... no preconceived ideas', the Aug-25 'more challenging than expected' EMEA comment, and the Middle East war comment).

STEPS:
(1) CourtListener / RECAP (free: https://www.courtlistener.com/?q=%22Dick%27s+Sporting+Goods%22 and the RECAP docket search for case 2:26-cv-01860 W.D. Pa.). Download every free docket entry (complaint, exhibits, notices of related cases, lead-plaintiff motions). Lead-plaintiff motions filed near 3-Nov may not exist yet; record the docket state as of today. Also look for any second-filed or related complaints (other law firms, other districts, e.g. S.D.N.Y. or D. Del.), derivative suits naming DKS directors, and any Foot Locker merger-disclosure suits.
(2) Read the complaint in full. Record: class period; alleged misstatements (exact quotes, speaker, date); alleged truth-revealing events and stock drops; every CW (role, location, employer such as 'former Foot Locker EMEA director', period employed) and what each says about inventory, promotions, store closures, international operations, integration, or plans for Europe/International. Note any allegation that management knew European performance was worse than stated.
(3) Law-firm press releases (Rosen, Pomerantz, Bernstein Liebhard, Levi & Korsinsky, Glancy, Faruqi, Bragar Eagel, Robbins Geller, etc.) often summarise the theory; use them only to locate the complaint and to note the stated class period and corrective disclosures.
(4) Other litigation touching FL Europe since 2025-09: search UK court lists (Business and Property Courts, e.g. landlord forfeiture or rent claims against Foot Locker U.K. Ltd or Freedom Sportsline), Find Case Law (caselaw.nationalarchives.gov.uk, free), and the EU General Court/CJEU (curia.europa.eu) for Foot Locker cases. Check the Delaware Court of Chancery for appraisal or fiduciary suits over the FL merger. Cluster C is covering European labour courts, so skip those.

OUTPUT: per item give court, case number, document and docket number, date, verbatim quote, the CW description if any, and why it bears on the theses. Tier A = court filing. If the complaint has nothing on international operations, say so explicitly: that is useful because it means plaintiffs' investigators found nothing on Europe.

tasks.title: Real-browser pass over merger-control registers that blocked scripts in wave 1 (Bundeskartellamt 2026, ACCC, EC case search, Hellenic/Romanian authorities)
tasks.instructions:
GOAL: Close the merger-control gaps left in wave 1, where the registers returned HTTP 403 or needed JavaScript. A notified acquisition of any Foot Locker business, stores or entity (by JD, Frasers, Snipes/Deichmann, Sport Vision, Fourlis, a private-equity buyer or anyone else) would be the hardest Tier A evidence for thesis 1 (DKS sells or licenses FL Europe/APAC). A null across all registers is useful AGAINST evidence. ALREADY KNOWN (not novel): Austria BWB/Z-6981 and Poland DKK-184/2025 cleared DKS/FL in 2025; the BWB register to 07.10.26 and 538 UOKiK entries contain no other FL case; the Bundeskartellamt 2025 archive has no FL entry; EC M.11159 (JD/Courir) mentions FL only as a competitor; no CMA case; JD/Cosmos Sport's notification of Sport Vision Greece to the Hellenic Competition Commission on 2-Oct-2026; Frasers/Hervis (Hungary, Romania).

STEPS (use a real browser tool if one is available; otherwise python requests with a full browser user-agent and normal headers; do NOT bypass CAPTCHAs or bot challenges):
(1) Germany: the Bundeskartellamt running-merger list 'Laufende Verfahren / Fusionskontrolle' for 2026 (https://www.bundeskartellamt.de/DE/Fusionskontrolle/LaufendeVerfahren/laufendeverfahren_node.html; also the downloadable 2026 list or PDF if one exists). Search for 'Foot Locker', 'Dick', 'Snipes', 'Deichmann', 'JD Sports', 'Frasers', 'Sport Vision', 'Schuhe', 'Sportartikel' and 'Einzelhandel mit Schuhen'. Germany has 79-82 FL stores, and a German store-portfolio purchase above the thresholds would be filed here. Record any footwear or sports-retail case with its number, parties, date and status.
(2) European Commission: competition-cases.ec.europa.eu search (JS-only) for party names 'Foot Locker' and 'DICK'S', and NACE G47.72 (retail sale of footwear) / G47.64 (sporting equipment) cases notified 2025-09 to today. Also check the EC 'prior notifications' published in the Official Journal C series (eur-lex) for 2026.
(3) Australia (APAC): the ACCC mandatory acquisitions register (live from 2026-01-01; https://www.accc.gov.au/public-registers/mergers-and-acquisitions-registers/acquisitions-register). Search 'Foot Locker', 'Accent', 'Frasers', 'Super Retail', 'JD Sports', 'Hype DC' and 'Platypus'. Any FL Australia sale would have to be notified. Record any notification touching FL or ANZ sneaker retail, with its date and status. Also check the NZ Commerce Commission clearance register for 2026.
(4) Greece and Romania: the Hellenic Competition Commission (epant.gr) and the Romanian Competition Council (consiliulconcurentei.ro) decision lists for 2025-26. Look for any Fourlis/Trade Estates or other filing involving Foot Locker stores or licences, and record the outcome and text of the JD/Sport Vision Greece case if published. Then the Italian AGCM weekly bulletin (Bollettino settimanale, 2026) and the Spanish CNMC 'concentraciones' list (2026), searched by name; wave 1 used only site searches there.
(5) For each register, give the URL, the search terms used, the date range covered, the number of entries scanned, and every relevant hit with its case number, date, parties, and an original-language quote with translation.

RULES: official registers only; no login, account creation or CAPTCHA bypass. Tier A = official register entry. Log a clean null per register explicitly.
